says: Hello, little chefs! It is Mango. Today we make a fluffy yellow omelet!
picture: Mango stands behind the light wooden kitchen counter, seen from the belly up, with one paw raised beside the head in a friendly wave. On the light wooden counter, left to right: one small white plate with two whole white eggs on it, one empty clear glass mixing bowl in the centre, one small metal whisk lying on the counter.
does: Mango waves the raised paw twice on 'Hello', lowers it, then points with one paw down at the two eggs on 'omelet'. The mouth opens and closes with every word. After the last word Mango closes the mouth and smiles.

says: First, crack two eggs into the bowl. Tap, tap, crack!
picture: Mango stands behind the light wooden kitchen counter, seen from the belly up. On the light wooden counter: a clear glass mixing bowl in the centre that already holds one raw egg, a round orange-yellow yolk in clear egg white; left of the bowl a small white plate with two empty half eggshells on it; right of the bowl a small metal whisk lying on the counter. Mango holds one whole white egg in both paws, touching the rim of the glass bowl.
does: Mango taps the whole egg twice on the rim of the glass bowl on 'Tap, tap'. On 'crack' the shell splits into two halves and the round yellow yolk with its clear egg white slides out of the shell and falls down into the bowl, next to the first yolk. Then Mango holds one empty half shell in each paw. The egg is seen falling from the shell into the bowl. Nothing appears from nowhere and nothing disappears. The mouth opens and closes with every word. After the last word Mango closes the mouth and smiles.

says: Now whisk, whisk, whisk, until it is all yellow.
picture: Mango stands behind the light wooden kitchen counter, seen from the belly up. On the light wooden counter: a clear glass mixing bowl in the centre holding two raw eggs, two round orange-yellow yolks in clear egg white; left of the bowl a small white plate with four empty half eggshells. Mango holds the small metal whisk in one paw with the wire end of the whisk inside the bowl, touching the yolks, and steadies the bowl with the other paw.
does: The paw moves the whisk round and round in quick small circles inside the bowl on each 'whisk'. The two yolks break and blend with the egg white until the bowl holds one smooth, even, pale yellow liquid on 'all yellow'. The whisk stays inside the bowl the whole time and nothing spills. The mouth opens and closes with every word. After the last word Mango stops whisking, closes the mouth and smiles.

says: The hot pan is a job for a grown-up. Pour it in, and wait.
picture: Mango stands behind a light wooden kitchen counter that has a flat black electric cooktop set into it, seen from the belly up. On the cooktop sits one round dark grey frying pan with its handle pointing to the side. There is no flame and no fire. Mango holds the clear glass mixing bowl, full of smooth pale yellow beaten egg, in both paws, tilted over the pan, and a thin stream of yellow egg has just begun to pour from the bowl into the pan.
does: Mango tilts the glass bowl further and the smooth yellow egg pours in a steady stream from the bowl into the frying pan, spreading into a round yellow layer that fills the pan, while the bowl empties. Then Mango puts the empty bowl down on the counter beside the cooktop on 'wait'. The egg is seen travelling from the bowl into the pan. No flame, no fire, no smoke. The mouth opens and closes with every word. After the last word Mango closes the mouth and smiles.

says: Look, a fluffy yellow omelet! Always cook with a grown-up. Bye-bye, little chefs!
picture: Mango stands behind the light wooden kitchen counter, seen from the belly up, with the whole teal apron and its round yellow pocket clearly visible. On the counter directly in front of Mango sits one round white plate with a single folded, fluffy, golden-yellow omelet on it. Mango points down at the omelet with one paw; the other paw rests on the counter. The counter is otherwise tidy and empty.
does: Mango taps the paw twice toward the omelet on 'Look', nods once on 'grown-up', then raises the same paw beside the head and waves on 'Bye-bye'. The plate with the single folded omelet stays still on the counter the whole time. The teal apron with its yellow pocket stays exactly as in the first frame, with no buttons. The mouth opens and closes with every word. After the last word Mango closes the mouth and smiles.
